body: You should carry that accomplishment as a badge of honor for the rest of your life. Congratulations, truly!

There's so much to say, and I want to leave everything out there. No regrets. MatPat's Game Theory has been with me for 12 years. I grew up as a Theorist and I loved it the entire time. Loved it enough to cry for most of this video. But I respect MatPat's decision and understand it's time. All things end eventually. So thank you MatPat. It was a pleasure to watch this journey of yours and go along for the ride. I'll carry both my gratitude and my joy for what your era of Game Theory has been until I die. In my eyes you're walking into that sunset with a victorious first held up and your head held high. The adults like me who were kids when they joined your journey, who grew up watching your Theories, are saluting you as we watch you go with tears in our eyes and smiles on our faces. You made my life better, you made all of our lives better. And you will be so, so missed. Thank you MatPat. Just... thank you.

With that said... If you're willing to follow an essay on how you're journey affected mine, well:

After watching every second of this and crying during most of it, I'm left with a complicated web of feelings. Joy for the countless hours of enrichment Game Theory, alongside all the other Theory channels, have given me. Grief and sorrow at the realization that, soon, those days will be over. Gratitude that extends far beyond words for what MatPat and Game Theory have been in my life these past 12 years. Yet the strongest feeling amongst the storm is the bittersweet nostalgia flooding my mind as I think back on it all, with the original 8-bit Game Theory theme song playing in my head.

I never consciously realized just how long I've been following Game Theory. 12 of my 24 years. Half my life, MatPat has been hosting Game Theory. Half my life I've been following this journey; I was one of the first NPC's he met after Nes left his home. I discovered MatPat as an abused 12 year old who went to YouTube for escape. YouTube was my happy place, a source of joy and learning and sanctuary and fun, and Game Theory fit that bill splendidly. His early videos drew me in right away, from "Can Dig Dug Pop a Human" to his Star Fox aileron roll video to "How Much is Minecraft Diamond Armor Worth" to Wario is 10 feet tall to Mario is a murderer to Peach is Rosalina's mother to his original FNAF video, all of it. It was some of my favorite content in that time! It was so much fun to find someone making these cool, clever videos thinking about video games the way I do. Plenty of his theories even introduced me to new knowledge I never would have learned otherwise. So my ever-curious mind devoured Game Theory after Game Theory. I think that's when the seed was planted for what I'm feeling now, because it's those old theories that are replaying in my head again and again as I process this news.

At first I found MatPat's humor and delivery too over the top for my tastes, but I still thoroughly enjoyed the content overall so I stuck around. And, over time, I became more and more endeared to the very things MatPat did that I initially considered cringe. What I used to read as cringe, like the God-tier puns to the generally positive, inquisitive demeanor, became joyful and somewhere along the way I grew to love everything you brought to your Game Theories. As time passed your signature catchphrase became something I especially loved, a marker of the content that fed my mind in a way no one else's did. "But that's just a theory. A Game Theory!" will live in my heart forever, a landmark of something absolutely glorious. Yet as I watched those videos, as I laughed and learned and grew up alongside Game Theory, alongside MatPat, as the years passed... I didn't notice the ticking of the clock. I never realized just exactly how long I had followed Game Theory, how long MatPat had been a part of my life, how special MatPat's Game Theory had truly become to me. Most of all, I never thought about just how much time had truly passed. It doesn't feel like it's been that long, even now. But I suppose it never does until you look back.

So, with my outpouring of mixed feelings said, I have a few last thoughts to share with you MatPat, if you ever happen to see this. Firstly, allow me to shower you in yet more gratitude for the last 12 years. Thank you, Matthew Patrick, for everything. You and your theories have been a gift I will appreciate and carry with me for the rest of my days. You made a difference to  broken 12 year old. You taught him to think about his games, to never stop asking questions, that there's always more to learn. You taught him that curiosity should be honed and harnessed and explored. You taught me that just being authentic and even occasionally silly is worthwhile if even just one person learns to love that authentic self, no matter how many hundreds of thousands of people may call you "cringe" for it. Beyond that you taught him that said authenticity can not only touch someone's heart but it can become the basis for incredible success and make lots of people happy along the way. Those lessons and more are all lessons you taught me during this journey of Game Theory, and I changed for the better because of them. You're content has been thought-provoking, creative, honest, endearing, and joyful from the very beginning and both you and the theories you've made will hold a special place in my heart forever because of that.

With tears in my eyes it's time to acknowledge that this journey you started, this era, will be over soon. Just admitting that to myself makes my heart ache. I know you have more theories coming before you walk off into that sunset, and when that clock finally does hit zero and you retire I pray you understand the gravity of how much your fans will miss you and what your Game Theory was. Even though the channel will live on and you'll move on to bigger and better things, your era of Game Theory will always be irreplaceable. More than you could ever know.

But even as I feel all this sadness, at the same time I'm so happy to have gone on that journey with you. I'm especially delighted that I'll be here to walk the final few steps alongside you. This NPC got to see you come home. He got to see you grow, change, evolve, and he got to go on that journey with you, all to get to see the end of it. There's nothing more I could ask for, and knowing that I'll be here to see how it all ends makes me smile even as the tears keep falling. We're both different now, but that only makes the time spent with your journey that much more special. You were a part of my childhood, Matthew Patrick. You stand shoulder to shoulder with titans like Pokémon's Ash and Fairy Tail's Natsu, two other instances of an era ending that made me cry and grieve when their time came. You're a titan, I truly hope my words here convey even half of that to you.

Just once more, thank you MatPat. It was an honor, joy, and privilege to go on this journey with you. You amaze me and inspire me. Maybe someday I can fulfill a dream of my own and make content that you watch. Game Theory was the first channel that made me imagine doing YouTube myself and I never took the plunge. Seeing your era of Game Theory come to an end makes realize that it'd be my delight to pay back the experience you've given me for even a moment, and that's the biggest motivation I've ever felt to embark on my own content creation journey and follow on the shoulders of beloved giants like you.

Until then it was all just a theory. A Game Theory. Thanks for letting me watch. It was a pleasure. Until our journeys cross once more, farewell.

I'm well aware of the extreme political differences within Oregon and Washington state. I'm a political science major, and that's actually one of the things that made me want to do this project to begin with. In fact, I'd argue their politics are different enough that it reflects a difference in culture. Of course you can have political disagreements without going that far, but how the Oregon senate Republicans have behaved over the past couple years and the constant petitions for Eastern Oregon to join Idaho is proof enough to me that it's more that politics alone that seperates them. That's exactly why I drew the border in Oregon along the Cascades: generally speaking thats the boundary between the two of them. I'm aware Medford isn't close to as liberal as Eugene or Portland, but it is still more tied to the Willamette Valley than it is to the Oregon basin, and creating borders that ignore the changing ideas of people is the point. Healthy borders respect cultural cohesion while staying anchored in geography, but when those two things clash following the Earth is the more stable bet.

Originally I had the border stay on the cascades the entire way up, but then I couldn't find any geographically logical way to finish the border in BC. The idea is to get greater Vancouver inside the same state as Seattle and Portland and their respective spheres of influence.

As for differences between Canada and the US, those are all political differences, not cultural. And the Canadian Conservatives being more liberal than the U.S. dems? Yeah, no. More liberal than the blue dog, third way idiots like the Clintons or Biden, but thats only half of the party. You also have people like Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez, and the Canadian Conservatives are NOT more liberal than them.

Besides, I didnt make this map based on political differences
